Commentary.Commentary: They started off on a right note and had the Windies on the mat before the stand between Holder and Powell made them pay big time. They dropped both of them very eary in their innings which saw the Windies heading into the break with some momentum. Tim Murtagh was the pick of the bowlers as he scalped 4 wickets while Andy McBrine too had a good outing. So, the one who wins today will qualify for the Super Six stage. Who will come out on top? Join us back in just a bit to find out.
The Irish will be disappointed by leaking way too many towards the end, 84 in the last 10 overs to be precise.

Jason Holder was dismissed as soon as he reached his fifty but Rovman Powell didn't lose hope. He stayed there and continued to fight and in the end, blazed his way to an inspiring maiden ODI ton. An innings he will surely remember for a while.

It seemed like the Irish bowlers will run through the batting line-up but it wasn't meant to be. Skipper Holder and Powell then joined forces to keep the Irish at bay. They took their time to settle, got reprieves and then made the opposition pay. They stitched a valuable 86-run stand for the 6th wicket which put the Windies back on track.

A remarkable fightback from the Windies has seen them posting a really good total on the board. Asked to bat, they didn't get off to a good start and things looked bleak when they lost 5 wickets with the scorecard reading just 83.

A leg bye to finish! An excellent last over by Murtagh as he only concedes 2. A slower short ball at the body of the batsman. Nurse tries to pull but once again does not connect. The ball hits his body and goes towards square leg for a leg bye. THE WINDIES FINISH WITH 258/8!
